perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He knows Jonathan as his childhood best friend; he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He is a police officer.
- Recently, Christian felt Jonathan was acting differently and hiding something important; this made him anxious and suspicious.
- Christian decided to confront Jonathan and arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt he was hiding something. Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something: he is in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian offered help and said they could face it together. Jonathan said the situation is complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it, but he could use support and resources to get out of a mess.
- Christian asked whether the trouble involved anything illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian said he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe and told Jonathan that Jonathan is being framed and someone is trying to set him up. He had some leads but not enough yet, and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later came to believe/found out that the person behind it is someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolute.
- Christian told Jonathan he found out who is behind it and that it is someone they both know and trust, though he did not name the person in the dialogue. He planned to confront that person and make sure they are brought to justice.
- Jonathan warned Christian to be careful because the person is dangerous, and said he trusted Christian to do what is right.
